# Movie dataset initial exploration before cleaning

[link to the description online](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets/doc/ggplot2movies/movies.html)
  
```{r initial exploration}
movies <- movies
head(movies)
dim(movies)
```


```{r cleaning and general statistics}
movies |> drop_na("budget") |> nrow() # 5215 of 58788, thus remove column unless interested in budget
# mpaa is not present for all, thus it is not a useful variable and removed

min(movies$year)
max(movies$year)

sum(is.na(movies$year)) # no missing values
sum(is.na(movies$rating))

# genre assignment with accounting for multiple assignments per movie
genres <- c("Action", "Animation", "Comedy", "Drama", "Documentary", "Romance")

clean_movies <- movies |>
  select(-budget, -mpaa) |>
  mutate(
    genre_combo = apply(
      pick(all_of(genres)), 1,
      \(x) paste(genres[as.logical(x)], collapse = " + ")
    ),
    genre = factor(ifelse(genre_combo == "", "None", genre_combo))
  )

# finding the highest and lowest rated movies on IMDB and their statistics

highest <- filter(clean_movies, rating == max(rating))
nrow(highest)
lowest  <- filter(clean_movies, rating == min(rating))
nrow(lowest)

highest_table <- clean_movies |> filter(clean_movies, rating == max(rating)) |>
  select(title, year, rating, votes, genre, length) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Highest rated movies on IMDB") |>
  cols_label(
    title = "Title",
    year  = "Year",
    rating = "Rating (1-10)",
    votes = "Votes",
    genre = "Genre",
    length = "Length (min)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = votes, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(columns = rating, decimals = 1) |>
  tab_style(
    style = list(cell_text(weight = "bold")),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  ) |>
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "Data from ggplot2's movies dataset.",
    locations = cells_title(groups = "title")
  )

highest_table

lowest_table <- lowest |>
  select(title, year, rating, votes, genre) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Lowest rated movies on IMDB") |>
  cols_label(
    title = "Title",
    year  = "Year",
    rating = "Rating",
    votes = "Votes",
    genre = "Genre"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = votes, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(columns = rating, decimals = 1) |>
  tab_style(
    style = list(cell_text(weight = "bold")),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  ) |>
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "Data from ggplot2's movies dataset.",
    locations = cells_title(groups = "title")
  )

lowest_table

# They have very few votes, thus I made other versions with votes above 100 and 1000
highest100 <- filter(clean_movies, votes > 100) |> filter(rating == max(rating))
nrow(highest100)
lowest100  <- filter(clean_movies, votes > 100) |> filter(rating == min(rating))
nrow(lowest100)

cat(str_glue(
  "Highest rated movie when filtering for more than 100 votes: \n {highest100$title} ({highest100$year})\n",
  "  Genre: {highest100$genre}\n",
  "  Rating: {highest100$rating} from {highest100$votes} votes\n\n",
  "Lowest rated movie when filtering for more than 100 votes:  \n {lowest100$title} ({lowest100$year})\n",
  "  Genre: {lowest100$genre}\n",
  "  Rating: {lowest100$rating} from {lowest100$votes} votes"
))
# function for cleanliness and robustness to multiple movies with the same rating instead: 
print_movies <- function(movies_df) {
  str_glue_data(movies_df,
    "{title} ({year})\n",
    "  Genre: {genre}\n",
    "  Rating: {rating} from {votes} votes\n"
  )
}

print_group <- function(label, movies_df) {
  cat(str_glue("\n{label}:\n\n",
               str_c(print_movies(movies_df), collapse = "\n\n")))
}

highest1000 <- filter(clean_movies, votes > 1000) |> filter(rating == max(rating))
nrow(highest1000)
lowest1000  <- filter(clean_movies, votes > 1000) |> filter(rating == min(rating))
nrow(lowest1000
